_about: Real accounts from four live investigation exports (2026-08-04), kept as the calibration
reference for the v10 recalibration of the Omi Analyst protocol.
WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. The suite cannot call the model, so nothing here asserts that a
future scan produces a particular score. What it does is (a) pin the deterministic checks
against prose the live model actually wrote, and (b) record, in one place, the accounts the
recalibration is supposed to move and the ones it must not touch, so the live re-scan has a
'live_score' is what the model returned BEFORE the recalibration. For must_come_down and
must_be_capped that number is the defect, not the target.
Metadata is copied from the export rows. A null means the export did not carry that column;
it is deliberately not guessed at, because inventing a figure is the exact failure this

_rule: Each of these clears the constitution's MECHANICAL GATE: a tell that can be quoted or stated
as a figure from the account's own cells. The recalibration must not drag them down, because
the gate was written to admit precisely this shape.

_rule: Every one of these was scored on repost share, topical narrowness, volume or tone, and
nothing else. All are long-lived accounts with an ordinary follower balance: the HEAVY
REPOSTER shape. Under the recalibration they cap at 49 unless a mechanical tell turns up in
their own cells, and none of the live assessments named one.
These are the rows that made the change necessary. 4ucmikey and Jillforhealth were published
as HIGH: an accusation, about a named person, on a fifteen-year-old account that retweets
politics.

_rule: The history ceiling. The old rule only covered a history that was never collected at all, so
a five-post sample was scored as though it were a pattern, and two accounts in identical
states (nothing collected) came out 31 points apart.
PedroJaniec at 3 and Jamison598294 at 34 are the same evidence: none. That spread is the
clearest possible demonstration that the number was not coming from the cells.

_rule: The most damaging class: a figure or a quotation carried from a neighbouring row into a
paragraph published about a different named person. The prose below is verbatim from the
live export, paired with the account's REAL metadata from its own row.
Both are caught deterministically today by grounding.check_figures, which is why they are
here as executable tests rather than as a note.

_rule: Not a prompt defect. The per-account tier was taken from the model unvalidated, so one export
rendered the same score under two different badges. Fixed in the join by deriving the tier
from the score.
Two of these were instructed by the prompt itself: the output contract asked for the score
counterfactual and permitted an alias in the prose. Both instructions are gone.
